script.help.title: Writing a script
script.help.intro: One line per thing that happens. Names are the ones of your characters, pictures, scenes, variables and items; anything unknown is underlined and can be created in one click.
script.help.speaksWithExpression: Mia speaks with an expression (if she is not on stage, she appears in the centre).
script.help.continuation: Two leading spaces: the line goes on (a new line in the same box).
script.help.background: The background changes from here on.
script.help.show: A character appears, or changes expression or place ({left} / {center} / {right}).
script.help.hide: A character leaves. “{hide} : {all}” makes everyone leave.
script.help.choice: A choice: the question (optional), then one option per line with the scene it leads to (none: the story goes on).
script.help.effects: Under an option: what it changes (add to a variable, set it, give or remove an item).
script.help.condition: A condition: where to go when it is true, and otherwise. Items: {item}, {without}.
script.help.conditionCases: Several cases: one line each, the first that is true wins. “{else} {if}” adds a case, “{else}” is for when none holds.
script.help.andOr: Several conditions in one case: “{and}” (all of them) or “{or}” (one of them), not both on a line.
script.help.optionCondition: Under an option: it only appears when this holds. Add “, {locked}” to show it greyed out instead of hiding it.
script.help.items: Gives or removes an item ({silent}: no notice).
script.help.end: An ending, with an optional short text below it.
script.help.note: A private note on the next line (never in the game).
script.help.literal: A line kept exactly as written, whatever it looks like.
script.help.heading: A scene (whole-game document only).
script.help.tipSlash: Type / at the start of a line to pick a command; names are suggested as you type.
script.help.tipCreate: ⌘. (Ctrl+.) creates every character, scene, variable and item named in the text.
script.help.tipPlay: ⌘⏎ (Ctrl+Enter) plays the game from the line under the cursor.
script.help.tipBrackets: Brackets are optional: [décor : Gare] and décor : Gare both work.
scriptImport.title: Import a script
scriptImport.intro: Paste a script, or open a text file. With # headings, each one becomes a scene of your game; without, the lines go at the end of the selected scene. Unknown names can then be created in one click.

tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to NovelWorks
tutorial.welcome.text: A quick tour of the editor, in a few steps. Nothing you do here changes your game. You can skip it at any time.
tutorial.scenes.title: Your scenes
tutorial.scenes.text: Your story is made of scenes, like chapters. Add and reorder them here. The other tabs hold your pictures, characters and variables.
tutorial.stage.title: The game screen
tutorial.stage.text: This is what players will see. Pick a background and set up the moment here. Text is typed directly in the text box.
tutorial.character.title: Add a character
tutorial.character.text: Put someone on stage with this button. Then drag them on the screen to place them and resize them.
tutorial.timeline.title: The moments
tutorial.timeline.text: A scene is a series of moments: a line of dialogue, a choice… Click a moment to edit it, and add new ones at the end.
tutorial.inspector.title: The details
tutorial.inspector.text: Everything about the selected item appears here: who is speaking, the music, what a choice leads to…
tutorial.play.title: Try your game
tutorial.play.text: Press Play to play from the title screen. “Play from here” starts at the moment you are editing.
tutorial.script.title: Visual or Script
tutorial.script.text: Prefer typing? Switch to Script to write a whole scene as text. Both views edit the same story.
tutorial.done.title: You are ready!
tutorial.done.text: Have fun creating. You can replay this tour anytime from the Help menu.
tutorial.assets.title: Import your pictures
tutorial.assets.text: Open the Assets tab, then press Import, or drop images from your computer onto the window. Choose a type for each one: background, character expression…
tutorial.background.title: Add a background
tutorial.background.text: Click here to choose the background of this moment. The window lists your backgrounds and lets you import a new picture right away. “Apply to the following moments” then keeps it for the rest of the scene.

tutorial.persist.title: Characters stay on stage
tutorial.persist.text: Like on a stage, characters stay in place until you change them: put Mia on at moment 4 and she is still there at the next moments. Your lines are not affected, only the background and the characters carry on. Choose “This moment only” here to keep a change to one moment. Under the moments, the chart shows who is on stage, and for how long.
tutorial.choices.title: Make your choices count
tutorial.choices.text: Add a Choice moment, then in an option press “Make the game remember something”: it can add to a Score (like Mia’s affection). Later, an “If…” moment sends the story to different scenes depending on the Score, with as many cases as you need. An option can also appear only when a condition holds. “Try it” shows where the story goes without playing.
tutorial.endings.title: See every ending
tutorial.endings.text: In Story map, with no scene selected, the panel on the right lists the endings of your game and what leads to each one. A warning tells you when an ending can’t be reached.
